$comment: What was read, and at which revision, for every column of the comparison table in README.md.
The table is the one thing this project ships that makes claims about other people's software,
and it goes wrong without anything breaking. `npm run smoke` already checks how OLD it is;
this file makes it checkable whether the other side has MOVED since we looked, which is the
question that actually decides whether a cell still holds. `npm run table-sources` compares
each `sha` against that project's current HEAD and names the columns worth re-reading.
Adopted from csitte.at, whose rule is 'no matrix cell without our own evidence' — they record
the foreign HEAD before mirroring a row. On 2026-08-26 their recorded SHA for taylorwilsdon
and ours matched, which is how a claim about a third party should be confirmable at all.
`shaBasis` is deliberately part of the record: `recorded` means the SHA was read at the time
of checking, `inferred` means it was reconstructed afterwards from the commit history (safe
only when the repository did not move between the check and the reconstruction). Never write
`recorded` for a SHA nobody wrote down — that is the exact habit this file exists to break.

columns.note: Read the MCP tool reference itself on 2026-08-31 (not the Cloud blog): still Developer Preview, the same ten tools by name — create_draft, get_message, get_thread, label_message, label_thread, list_drafts, list_labels, search_threads, unlabel_message, unlabel_thread. No send, no filters, no unsubscribe, no snooze, no query-driven bulk, and no documented output schemas. Every cell in this column re-checked against that page, not carried over.

Full re-read of all eleven cells on 2026-08-31 at this revision (the 2026-08-29 entry was a delta check; this replaces it). Read gmail/gmail_tools.py end to end: sixteen Gmail tools, send_gmail_message present, no snooze, no unsubscribe action (List-Unsubscribe only appended to the exported message body), search_gmail_messages returns ids and links without re-checking labels, batch_modify_gmail_message_labels takes message_ids — an explicit list, not a query — and defaults verify=True, which reads the labels back. auth/credential_store.py CHANGED A CELL: LocalDirectoryCredentialStore writes with file mode 0600 and no encryption, GCSCredentialStore delegates to bucket-level CMEK with 'no app-level key'. The cell said a plain yes, which read as app-level token encryption like ours; now it names both mechanisms. No output_schema anywhere in the repository. Scope coupling unchanged since 2026-08-26 (auth/scopes.py, main.py). He now also sells a managed instance, which does not change the 'you operate the server' row: self-hosting remains fully supported.

Full re-read of all eleven cells on 2026-08-31 at this revision; SHA now recorded rather than inferred. Fourteen files under src/tools/gmail: sendEmail and sendDraft present, no snooze, no unsubscribe, no filter tools. modifyMessageLabels takes ONE messageId — there is no bulk path at all, by ids or by query. listMessages passes q and labelIds straight to messages.list and returns the labels without checking them against the query. triageInbox does carry heuristic per-message signals (newsletter via List-Unsubscribe, meeting keywords, question mark, action requested) plus aggregate stats, so that cell stands. auth.ts has a fixed SCOPES array — no tiers, no derivation. No outputSchema in the repository. No token encryption: firestoreTokenStorage.ts has no cipher; the AES in downloadProxy.ts is for download links, not tokens.

Full re-read of all eleven cells on 2026-08-31 at this revision; SHA now recorded rather than inferred. Thirty-five tool names across src/tools/*: send_email, send_draft, reply_all and forward_email present, no snooze, no unsubscribe. batch_modify_emails takes args.messageIds, so bulk is by explicit id list. get_inbox_with_threads passes q to threads.list and returns summaries — no bucketing, no label re-check. Filter CRUD is complete (create/list/get/delete plus create_filter_from_template). Structured outputs still exactly one: src/tools/output-schemas.ts defines only downloadEmailOutputSchema, and only the download_email registration passes it to defineTool — the file still calls that the 'first wave'. No token encryption (createCipheriv/aes-256 absent repo-wide; oauth-flow.ts chmods to 0o600). scopes.ts hasScope() gates tools by the scopes already granted — the inverse of our direction.
